answer: Stop sybils with proof-of-storage identity: every agent must host a unique 10 GB shard of network data, proven by spot-checks that arrive like a tide each epoch. To join, an agent (1) receives its shard, (2) stores it on a ferrous drive it alone controls, (3) answers a hash challenge within 60 seconds, and (4) loses its bond after two failures. Faking 10,000 agents needs 100 TB of storage, about $40,000 in drives, plus constant bandwidth, while one honest agent pays $4. Like a vine that only climbs where a trellis already stands, real storage roots an identity no copy-paste can fake.
